entries.en: We lost contact yesterday. Now I can't get clearance to check it out - suddenly it's a restricted area.
I appreciate that, Commander. I was running out of options.
Well, that's more than most will commit to.
I'm going to stay here and see if I can find anything out through official channels. Won't hold my breath, though.
I'll upload the info on where my team was last seen to your ship. Maybe you can get some answers.
I'm just waiting for someone, Commander.
Come and see me later, Commander. I'm busy right now.
Not now, Commander.
Not yet, Admiral.
Captain Anderson said you had information on Banes.
You should have mentioned this earlier, Admiral.
I appreciate that.
Is something wrong, Admiral?
Captain Anderson said you'd have information on Banes.
I'll find them, Admiral.
I'll look for them if I have time.
I have to go, Admiral.
Why didn't you tell me?
Problems
Banes
Commander Shepard, isn't it? My name is Admiral Kahoku. Is there something I can do for you?
Commander. Any word on my missing men?
I'm a senior officer with the Alliance. I knew about your candidacy before the Normandy was sent to Eden Prime.
Yes - that's right. They went missing a few days ago. I've been trying to find out what happened to them, but I keep getting the run around from Alliance brass.
Do you know something about this, Commander?
A... a thresher maw? That's not... my men wouldn't just stumble into a thresher nest! Not the entire unit!
Damn it! I had a bad feeling about this ever since my team disappeared. An Alliance beacon used as bait, my unit wiped out... and nobody seems to know anything about it!
Commander, I appreciate what you did. Now I need to do my part. The families of those marines deserve to know why they died.
Not right now, Shepard. But I'll let you know as soon as I find something out.
I will, Shepard. I'll let you know when I find anything out.
You've already done enough, Shepard. The rest is up to me.
Banes is already dead. It's too late for him. I'm only concerned about my team. Someone has to find them.
Please, Shepard. I'm counting on you.
But that doesn't apply to you, Shepard. Spectres can go anywhere they want. You could find out why my team dropped out of contact.
Sorry, I don't think we've met.
Who told you I was a Spectre?
You sent a recon team out into the Artemis Tau cluster?
I'm not sure how to tell you this, Admiral. Your men were killed by a thresher maw.
They were killed by a thresher maw.
I found them. What was left of them. They ran into a thresher maw.
Somebody lured them there with an Alliance distress beacon. Placed it perfectly so they'd land right beside the thresher nest.
Anything you need from me?
I hope you find what you're after, Admiral.
I found your men.
I've got bad news.
They're dead.
It wasn't their fault.
They were set up.
It was a trap.
How do you know about that?
No. I'm waiting to speak with one of the Councilor's assistants.
No. I just want to ask a couple of questions.
No. I haven't spoken to him before. This is the first time I've requested an audience.
Yeah, I'll wait. Doesn't seem like I have much choice.
Yes. I'm still waiting.
This is it: the very heart of the Citadel. The pinnacle of galactic power. Kind of makes your head spin if you think about it too much.
So this is where the Council passes judgment on all us little folk, huh? Ever get the feeling we're in over our heads, Commander?
Think of all the important decisions the Council has made right here. Trillions of lives hanging on their every word and deed. It is awe-inspiring!
Through all my time at C-Sec, I-- I never got the chance to witness a meeting of the Council in person.
I've always wondered if the turians released the genophage on their own, or if the Council secretly encouraged them.
Three hundred years ago, the geth drove my people into exile. We asked the Council to wipe the synthetics out, but they ignored our pleas.
Maybe if they'd listened, we wouldn't be here now.
The hearing's already started.  Come on.
Come on. Udina's presenting the quarian's evidence to the Council.
It was a mistake bringing you into that hearing, Captain. You and Saren have too much history. It made the Council question our motives.
I know Saren. He's working with the geth for one reason: to exterminate the entire human race.
Every colony we have is at risk. Every world we control is in danger. Even Earth isn't safe.
I worked with him on a mission a long time ago. Things went bad. Real bad.
We shouldn't talk about this here. But I know what he's like. And he has to be stopped.
As a Spectre, he's virtually untouchable. We need to find some way to expose him.
What about Garrus, that C-Sec investigator? We saw him arguing with the executor.
That's right! He was asking for more time to finish his report. Seems like he was close to finding something on Saren.
Not all turians are like Saren. If he can help, we need to find him.
I have a contact in C-Sec who can help us track Garrus down. His name is Harkin.
Forget it. They suspended Harkin last month. Drinking on the job. I won't waste my time with that loser.
You won't have to. I don't want the Council using your past history with Saren as an excuse to ignore anything we turn up. Shepard will handle this.
The ambassador's right. I need to step aside.
I need to take care of some business. Captain, meet me in my office later.
Tell me about this history between you and Saren.
What's our next step?
We need to deal with Saren ourselves.
He's a turian. I don't want him on our side.
Any idea where we could find him?
You can't just cut Captain Anderson out of this investigation.
I'll take care of it.
How do you know Saren?
The Council won't help us.
I don't trust him.
He could be useful.
The captain deserves better.
The hearing's already started. Come on.
The geth attack is a matter of some concern. But there is nothing to indicate Saren was involved in any way.
The investigation by Citadel Security turned up no evidence to support your charge of treason.
An eyewitness saw him kill Nihlus in cold blood!
We've read the Eden Prime reports, Ambassador. The testimony of one traumatized dockworker is hardly compelling proof.
I resent these accusations. Nihlus was a fellow Spectre. And a friend.
That just let you catch him off guard!
Captain Anderson. You always seem to be involved when humanity makes false charges against me.
And this must be your protégé, Commander Shepard. The one who let the beacon get destroyed.
With Nihlus gone, his files passed on to me. I read the Eden Prime report. I was unimpressed.
Shift the blame to cover your own failures, just like Captain Anderson. He's taught you well.
But what can you expect from a human?
He has no right to say that! That's not his decision!
Shepard's admission into the Spectres is not the purpose of this meeting.
This meeting has no purpose. The humans are wasting your time, Councilor. And mine.
There is still one outstanding issue: Commander Shepard's vision. It may have been triggered by the beacon.
I agree. Our judgment must be based on facts and evidence, not wild imaginings and reckless speculation.
The Council has found no evidence of any connection between Saren and the geth. Ambassador, your petition to have him disbarred from the Spectres is denied.
I'm glad to see justice was served.
This meeting is adjourned.
The mission to Eden Prime was top secret. The only way you could know about the beacon was if you were there!
You're the one who destroyed the beacon. Then you tried to cover it up.
You can expect me to kill you the next time we meet.
You can't hide behind the Council forever!
You've made your decision. I won't waste my breath.
How did you get involved?
That was you, not me!
You'll pay!
I'll find proof!
You won't see the truth.
What's the point?
Your species needs to learn its place, Shepard. You're not ready to join the Council. You're not even ready to join the Spectres!
What we need is evidence. So far, we have seen nothing.
Are we allowing dreams into evidence now? How can I defend my innocence against this kind of testimony?
Do you have anything else to add, Commander Shepard?
Saren despises humanity. That's why he attacked Eden Prime!
Saren's hiding behind his position as a Spectre. You need to open your eyes!
Insults? Typical.
See? He hates us!
Quit protecting him!
You arrogant bastard!
Spectres bear a great burden. They are protectors of galactic peace, both our first and last line of defense. The safety of the galaxy is theirs to uphold.
You are the first human Spectre, Commander. This is a great accomplishment for you and your entire species.
We're sending you into the Traverse after Saren. He's a fugitive from justice, so you are authorized to use any means necessary to apprehend or eliminate him.
We will forward any relevant files to Ambassador Udina.
This meeting of the Council is adjourned.
We've got a lot of work to do, Shepard. You're going to need a ship, a crew, supplies...
Anderson, come with me. I'll need your help to set all this up.
I thought the ambassador would be a little more grateful. He didn't even thank you.
I expected your ambassador to be more grateful. He didn't even thank you.
Hmph! Bastard didn't even thank you.
Not even a thank you from the ambassador.
Right behind you, Commander.
You wanted proof. There it is.
I recognize the other voice, the one speaking with Saren. Matriarch Benezia.
Matriarchs are powerful asari who have entered the final stage of their lives. Revered for their wisdom and experience, they serve as guides and mentors to my people.
Matriarch Benezia is a powerful biotic, and she had many followers. She will make a formidable ally for Saren.
I'm more interested in the Reapers. What do you know about them?
Only what was extracted from the geth's memory core. The Reapers were an ancient race of machines that wiped out the Protheans. Then they vanished.
We think the Conduit is the key to bringing them back. Saren's searching for it. That's why he attacked Eden Prime.
